currentContext.strengths: Pioneer of radial tyre technology in India with a long-standing technology-led positioning|Extensive pan-India distribution — ~900 outlets, 6,000+ dealer partners, 700+ dealer additions during the year, covering over 90% of India by geography|Smart/connected-tyre technology via the TREEL platform — India's first embedded smart passenger car tyres, ~11 million data points/month|Majority share in the EV bus segment with OEM-accepted EV-specific tyres (Jetway JUXe)|Strong brand and motorsport-led positioning (Levitas, Guinness World Record drift, Formula 2-winning protege driver)|Retreading network (JK Treads, 90+ centres, 450+ customers) extending tyre life and lowering customer cost per kilometre|In-house R&D capability via the Raghupati Singhania Centre of Excellence (RPSCOE), Mysuru|Diversified international manufacturing base in Mexico (JK Tornel) providing access to American markets
currentContext.strategies: Sweat existing/matured manufacturing assets to high utilisation (crossed 90% in key segments) before layering on fresh growth capex|Premiumisation-led mix improvement across PCR, farm, truck/bus and 2/3-wheeler segments, including higher rim-size and performance-tyre participation|Selective, margin-focused international growth — in JK Tornel (Mexico) export decisions are guided by profitability and portfolio discipline rather than headline volume, avoiding price-led competition against low-cost global substitutes|Scale the connected/smart-tyre mobility platform (TREEL) — embedding sensing and data intelligence into tyres for safety and performance monitoring|Shift from product-led selling to integrated lifecycle fleet management in Truck & Bus, via the Mobility Solutions platform and digital fleet-service interventions|R&D-led material innovation aimed at decoupling growth from resource intensity — expanding sustainable/circular material usage (e.g., UX Green tyres made with 80% sustainable material) broadly across product categories rather than a few flagship SKUs, while preserving performance|Expand rural distribution footprint via a new Rural Business vertical and Rural Distributor appointments into previously unrepresented markets|Deepen pan-India channel network through dealer additions and branded retail/Steel Wheels outlet expansion|In Mexico, strengthen domestic distribution, sharpen product mix and expand capacity ahead of demand as a structural response to tariff and currency volatility|Digital-first, measurement-led brand building with sharper segment-specific communication across passenger, truck and farm categories|The Board reviews long-term strategy and growth roadmap, capital expenditure plans and funding mix, risk management frameworks and sustainability targets/disclosures as part of its oversight. During the year, governance focus centred on capital efficiency (monitoring commissioning and ramp-up of newly installed capacities and ensuring targeted utilisation levels), debt optimisation (replacing higher-cost borrowings with lower-cost and foreign-currency debt while maintaining liquidity buffers), and risk preparedness for raw-material volatility, trade-tariff disruptions and capacity constraints through proactive planning. Board deliberations emphasised operational leverage, margin resilience and balance-sheet strength, ensuring growth initiatives remain aligned with financial prudence. The Notice of the AGM includes an item to declare a dividend, though no payout ratio or per-share figure is present in this text bundle.
currentContext.expansion: Manufacturing focus shifted during the year from capacity creation to capacity optimisation, with recent investments across PCR, TBR and all-steel LCV radial driving stronger utilisation, throughput and mix quality. Phase III of the Banmore passenger car radial expansion was inaugurated on 14th January 2026, raising Banmore capacity to 30,000 tyres per day (about 10.5 million tyres annually). Expansion projects with a ₹1,400 crore outlay — the Banmore PCR expansion and the Laksar Truck Bus Radial (TBR) expansion — were commissioned during the year and are currently under ramp-up, with full utilisation expected by Q1 FY 2026-27. Capacity building also continued via all-steel radial additions and Mexico (JK Tornel) plant modernisation. In Mexico, JK Tornel initiated a US$75 million expansion programme (Phase I: US$27.5 million) to add ultra-modern manufacturing machines including uniformity systems, a new northern warehouse focused on over-16-inch rim-size tyres, and an expanded high-margin ATV portfolio; Phase I is scheduled for completion by July 2026. On the raw-material side, natural-rubber localisation is being advanced through Project INROAD, with nearly 90% of identified North-East plantations showing progress and production expected to begin from mid-2030.
currentContext.mdna: Domestic demand tailwind from India's GDP growth (over 7% in FY26, expected to remain above 6% in FY27), infrastructure/Gati Shakti capex and GST 2.0 rate rationalisation, which cut GST on Commercial Vehicles, small cars and tractors and had a positive rub-off on OEM tyre demand|Indian tyre industry recorded double-digit growth in FY26 and is expected to roughly quadruple over the next two decades in line with the 'Viksit Bharat 2047' vision, supported by a large vehicle base, logistics/e-commerce growth, infrastructure expansion, premiumisation and radialisation|Growth remained largely domestic/aftermarket-led; exports faced headwinds from tariff uncertainty, geopolitical volatility, logistics disruptions and high freight costs|Raw material cost risk: inputs (over 60% of tyre cost) depend on imported natural and synthetic rubber; volatility rose toward year-end on a depreciating Rupee and higher crude prices, and the long-standing inverted duty structure remains unresolved|FY27 industry outlook is positive but with moderate growth; material input costs are likely to escalate and new regulatory norms (CAFE III, BS7, TREM V) are likely to add further cost pressure over the long run|Elevated geopolitical uncertainty (West Asia war) is an emerging headwind showing early signs of moderating growth|Premiumisation and radialisation continue as structural demand drivers — SUV mix shift in PVs, entry-level to premium shift in 2W, and EV penetration doubling to ~4% in PVs and reaching ~7% in 2W|Commercial vehicle segment demand supported by infrastructure projects, GST 2.0 logistics streamlining and scrappage-policy enforcement; bus electrification rising, led by State Transport Undertakings|In Mexico, tariff and currency volatility are treated as a now-structural feature of global trade, prompting a deliberate emphasis on domestic distribution strength, product-mix sharpening and capacity built ahead of demand|JK Tornel (Mexico) commenced OE supplies to Kia Mexico during the year, with additional SKUs planned, extending its OEM relationship pipeline in the North American market

risks.note: The tyre industry's global integration exposes raw-material sourcing and export access to geopolitical shocks and trade protectionism (higher tariffs, instability), bringing supply-chain disruption and demand volatility that could slow the post-pandemic economic recovery.

risks.risk: Raw material cost and supply volatility (crude-linked inputs)
risks.note: Crude-linked raw material prices saw heightened volatility toward the end of FY26 due to geopolitical upheavals, including a March 2026 Strait of Hormuz-linked disruption, directly straining the global supply landscape and cost stability.

A critical Natural Rubber deficit of 35% still persists in India; the Company's multi-year 'Inroad Project' rubber-plantation initiative in Northeast India (now in its fifth year) only partially bridges the domestic supply-demand gap, leaving continued reliance on imports.

International business is shaped by trade protectionism, tariff uncertainty and geopolitical volatility, requiring a selective, region-led, margin-conscious export strategy (pricing discipline, receivable security) rather than volume-led growth.

As digital integration deepens across manufacturing, customer interfaces, service systems and connected-product platforms, information security and system reliability become more material risk domains for the enterprise.

risks.risk: Competitive intensity in the tyre industry
risks.note: JK Tyre operates in a competitive industry facing multiple risks across financial, operational, sectoral, ESG, IT and cyber domains that could impact operations and financial performance, requiring sustained cost control, strategic diversification and R&D investment to mitigate.

one-line thesis: JK Tyre delivered record FY26 profitability with 270 bps margin expansion in Q4 driven by volume growth and mix, but faces immediate Q1FY27 headwinds from an 18-20% raw material cost surge due to geopolitical tensions. Management is countering this with staggered price hikes and committing to a massive Rs 6,110 crore capex plan through FY29 to alleviate >90% capacity utilization, signaling strong confidence in long-term structural demand despite short-term inflationary noise.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Rs 4,233 Cr (Q4, +12% YoY), Rs 16,384 Cr (FY26, +11% YoY); EBITDA: Rs 546 Cr (Q4, +42% YoY), Margin 12.9% (+270 bps YoY); PAT: Rs 188 Cr (Q4, +83% YoY), Rs 774 Cr (FY26, +50% YoY); Order Book: No specific volume order book disclosed, but management confirms no OEM order cuts and full capacity utilization (>90%); Net Debt: Rs 4,445 Cr (up Rs 364 Cr YoY due to expansion loans), Net Debt/EBITDA improved to 2.13x. One-offs: Other income declined sequentially as QIP funds (Rs 700+ Cr) were deployed from fixed deposits into capex projects.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Mid-single digit expected for FY27 auto industry; Margins: Under pressure in Q1FY27 due to 18-20% RM cost hike, mitigated by 4-7% price hikes already taken and further 5-6% planned; Order Inflow: Buoyant demand expected, no OEM cancellations; Capex: Rs 1,200 Cr outlay for FY27, part of Rs 6,110 Cr total expansion (Rs 1,130 Cr ongoing + Rs 4,980 Cr new) to complete by FY29.
order book & pipeline: No explicit numerical order book provided; qualitative indicators show full capacity utilization (>90%) across segments, robust OEM approvals (Tata, Ashok Leyland, Mahindra, etc.), and no order cancellations despite geopolitical uncertainty.
segment / subsidiary detail: TBR: Replacement +19%, OE +53% YoY; PCR: Replacement +10%, OE +26% YoY (Premium 16'+ grew 13%); Farm: +58% YoY (OE nearly doubled); 2/3W: OE +72%, Replacement +39% QoQ. Market Mix Q4: 63% Replacement, 27% OE, 10% Export. Category Mix: TBR 56%, PCR 27%, Non-Truck Bias 13%, 2/3W 4%.
growth verticals / optionality: Rs 4,980 Cr new brownfield expansion approved to increase TBR & PCR capacity by 24% by FY29; Premiumization strategy (Shresth Plus, Levitas Ultra) driving higher realizations; 'Selling Miles' fleet management program creating sticky B2B relationships; Outsourcing strategy to rapidly scale 2/3W segment without heavy asset investment.
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 RM basket +1.3% QoQ, flat YoY; Q1FY27 RM costs projected to surge 18-20% due to West Asia crisis and rupee weakness. Mitigation: 4-5% price hike in domestic replacement, 5-7% in exports already implemented; additional 5-6% hike underway. OEM price increases will lag. Management expects crude softening post-Q2 to ease pressure.
capex / expansion: Total Rs 6,110 Cr planned through FY29 (Rs 1,130 Cr announced previously + Rs 4,980 Cr new). FY27 cash outlay ~Rs 1,200 Cr. Funding via mix of debt (target D:E ~2:1 for projects) and internal accruals (expected cash generation >Rs 1,600 Cr annually).
capital allocation: Debt utilized for expansion (Net Debt up Rs 364 Cr to Rs 4,445 Cr); Working capital borrowings reduced significantly (Rs 2,378 Cr to Rs 1,808 Cr); Cash balance decreased to Rs 301 Cr from Rs 711 Cr as QIP funds deployed into capex; Focus on maintaining comfortable leverage ratios (Net Debt/EBITDA 2.13x).
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical instability (West Asia) causing raw material volatility and supply chain disruptions; Potential demand moderation in H2FY27 if price hikes are not fully passed through; Trade uncertainty in Mexico (US tariffs, USMCA review); Intense competition from new entrants in TBR/PCR segments.
management quality / tone: Confident and aggressive on growth (record volumes, massive capex commitment) but cautious on near-term margins due to external macro shocks; Emphasizes operational discipline, premiumization, and digital transformation (AI) as key moats.
non-obvious takeaways: Management explicitly highlighted 'Agentic AI' deployment for decision-making and workflow automation, moving beyond basic analytics; The 'Selling Miles' fleet management program is positioned as a significant entry barrier against new competitors by creating service-based stickiness rather than just product sales; Mexico subsidiary (JK Tornel) facing sluggishness due to US tariff uncertainty despite stable full-year revenue.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Surge in raw material costs (18-20%) pressuring margins for players unable to pass on prices quickly. | JK Tyre & Industries Ltd | beneficiary | High | Already implemented 4-7% price hikes and has strong premium mix to absorb shock; full capacity utilization allows immediate monetization of any demand. |
| Capacity constraints limiting growth for competitors without immediate expansion plans. | JK Tyre & Industries Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Massive Rs 6,110 Cr capex plan positions them to capture market share as demand grows, though execution risk exists. |
| US tariff uncertainty and trade tensions affecting Mexican manufacturing exports. | JK Tornel (Subsidiary) | loser | Med | Q4 sluggishness attributed to geopolitical volatility; reliance on USMCA renewal creates near-term overhang. |

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Domestic demand tailwind from India's GDP growth (over 7% in FY26, expected to remain above 6% in FY27), infrastructure/Gati Shakti capex and GST 2.0 rate rationalisation, which cut GST on Commercial Vehicles, small cars and tractors and had a positive rub-off on OEM tyre demand
- Indian tyre industry recorded double-digit growth in FY26 and is expected to roughly quadruple over the next two decades in line with the 'Viksit Bharat 2047' vision, supported by a large vehicle base, logistics/e-commerce growth, infrastructure expansion, premiumisation and radialisation
- Growth remained largely domestic/aftermarket-led; exports faced headwinds from tariff uncertainty, geopolitical volatility, logistics disruptions and high freight costs
- Raw material cost risk: inputs (over 60% of tyre cost) depend on imported natural and synthetic rubber; volatility rose toward year-end on a depreciating Rupee and higher crude prices, and the long-standing inverted duty structure remains unresolved
- FY27 industry outlook is positive but with moderate growth; material input costs are likely to escalate and new regulatory norms (CAFE III, BS7, TREM V) are likely to add further cost pressure over the long run
- Elevated geopolitical uncertainty (West Asia war) is an emerging headwind showing early signs of moderating growth
- Premiumisation and radialisation continue as structural demand drivers — SUV mix shift in PVs, entry-level to premium shift in 2W, and EV penetration doubling to ~4% in PVs and reaching ~7% in 2W
- Commercial vehicle segment demand supported by infrastructure projects, GST 2.0 logistics streamlining and scrappage-policy enforcement; bus electrification rising, led by State Transport Undertakings
- In Mexico, tariff and currency volatility are treated as a now-structural feature of global trade, prompting a deliberate emphasis on domestic distribution strength, product-mix sharpening and capacity built ahead of demand
- JK Tornel (Mexico) commenced OE supplies to Kia Mexico during the year, with additional SKUs planned, extending its OEM relationship pipeline in the North American market

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Q4 RM basket +1.3% QoQ, flat YoY; Q1FY27 RM costs projected to surge 18-20% due to West Asia crisis and rupee weakness. Mitigation: 4-5% price hike in domestic replacement, 5-7% in exports already implemented; additional 5-6% hike underway. OEM price increases will lag. Management expects crude softening post-Q2 to ease pressure.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Debt utilized for expansion (Net Debt up Rs 364 Cr to Rs 4,445 Cr); Working capital borrowings reduced significantly (Rs 2,378 Cr to Rs 1,808 Cr); Cash balance decreased to Rs 301 Cr from Rs 711 Cr as QIP funds deployed into capex; Focus on maintaining comfortable leverage ratios (Net Debt/EBITDA 2.13x).

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Manufacturing focus shifted during the year from capacity creation to capacity optimisation, with recent investments across PCR, TBR and all-steel LCV radial driving stronger utilisation, throughput and mix quality. Phase III of the Banmore passenger car radial expansion was inaugurated on 14th January 2026, raising Banmore capacity to 30,000 tyres per day (about 10.5 million tyres annually). Expansion projects with a ₹1,400 crore outlay — the Banmore PCR expansion and the Laksar Truck Bus Radial (TBR) expansion — were commissioned during the year and are currently under ramp-up, with full utilisation expected by Q1 FY 2026-27. Capacity building also continued via all-steel radial additions and Mexico (JK Tornel) plant modernisation. In Mexico, JK Tornel initiated a US$75 million expansion programme (Phase I: US$27.5 million) to add ultra-modern manufacturing machines including uniformity systems, a new northern warehouse focused on over-16-inch rim-size tyres, and an expanded high-margin ATV portfolio; Phase I is scheduled for completion by July 2026. On the raw-material side, natural-rubber localisation is being advanced through Project INROAD, with nearly 90% of identified North-East plantations showing progress and production expected to begin from mid-2030.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and aggressive on growth (record volumes, massive capex commitment) but cautious on near-term margins due to external macro shocks; Emphasizes operational discipline, premiumization, and digital transformation (AI) as key moats.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Pioneer of radial tyre technology in India with a long-standing technology-led positioning
- Extensive pan-India distribution — ~900 outlets, 6,000+ dealer partners, 700+ dealer additions during the year, covering over 90% of India by geography
- Smart/connected-tyre technology via the TREEL platform — India's first embedded smart passenger car tyres, ~11 million data points/month
- Majority share in the EV bus segment with OEM-accepted EV-specific tyres (Jetway JUXe)
- Strong brand and motorsport-led positioning (Levitas, Guinness World Record drift, Formula 2-winning protege driver)
- Retreading network (JK Treads, 90+ centres, 450+ customers) extending tyre life and lowering customer cost per kilometre
- In-house R&D capability via the Raghupati Singhania Centre of Excellence (RPSCOE), Mysuru
- Diversified international manufacturing base in Mexico (JK Tornel) providing access to American markets

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Geopolitical instability (West Asia) causing raw material volatility and supply chain disruptions; Potential demand moderation in H2FY27 if price hikes are not fully passed through; Trade uncertainty in Mexico (US tariffs, USMCA review); Intense competition from new entrants in TBR/PCR segments.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Management explicitly highlighted 'Agentic AI' deployment for decision-making and workflow automation, moving beyond basic analytics; The 'Selling Miles' fleet management program is positioned as a significant entry barrier against new competitors by creating service-based stickiness rather than just product sales; Mexico subsidiary (JK Tornel) facing sluggishness due to US tariff uncertainty despite stable full-year revenue.

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Surge in raw material costs (18-20%) pressuring margins for players unable to pass on prices quickly. | JK Tyre & Industries Ltd | beneficiary | High | Already implemented 4-7% price hikes and has strong premium mix to absorb shock; full capacity utilization allows immediate monetization of any demand. |
| Capacity constraints limiting growth for competitors without immediate expansion plans. | JK Tyre & Industries Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Massive Rs 6,110 Cr capex plan positions them to capture market share as demand grows, though execution risk exists. |
| US tariff uncertainty and trade tensions affecting Mexican manufacturing exports. | JK Tornel (Subsidiary) | loser | Med | Q4 sluggishness attributed to geopolitical volatility; reliance on USMCA renewal creates near-term overhang. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [R&D] "Asia's first & India's foremost highly versatile R&D Centre with advanced testing and evaluation machines", staffed by "250+ Scientists and Engineers", with "7 Patents granted" across advanced/alternate materials, nanotechnology, process and product simulation, predictive technology and tyre mechanics.
- [R&D infrastructure] "India's biggest Anechoic Chamber for Noise and Vibration analysis" and the "First Industry academia tie-up with IIT-Madras (since 2004)".
- [Group structure] Overseas manufacturing sits under JK Tornel in Mexico (2 plants: Hidalgo, Tultitlan), so consolidated figures in the deck span India plus Mexico while standalone figures cover the Indian entity only.
- [Filing] The document is a Regulation 30 intimation dated 7th August 2026 enclosing the Q1FY27 Investor Presentation (BSE Scrip Code 530007, NSE Symbol JKTYRE).
